subject: Proof of Operation & Maintainability for private deployment — PoC and runbook request
messages:
From: Alice Dunne <alice.dunne@pivothealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@pivothealth.com>, procurement@pivothealth.com
Date: 2025-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — request for PoC proof-of-operation and maintainability details

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we progress the procurement side at Pivot Health we need a short packet that proves how Redwood would operate in our VPC/on‑prem environment for the procurement committee and our security team. Specifically they asked for: 

- A concise PoC runbook (operator steps to stand up, verify, and tear down) we can walk through in a 2‑day pilot.
- Failover and switchover scenarios with expected RTO/RPO and step‑by‑step operator commands.
- A sample maintenance plan (patching windows, rollback instructions, operator oncall matrix).
- Network diagram showing egress controls and what the on‑prem installer communicates to Redwood (if anything).
- Evidence that operator credentials and KV material can be rotated without service disruption.

Can your team provide the PoC runbook and a short narrative addressing the points above by end of week? Procurement also wants one PDF they can attach to the RFP response.

Best,
Alice
Director of IT Ops 
Pivot Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Dunne <alice.dunne@pivothealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request for PoC proof-of-operation and maintainability details

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely produce a concise packet and a runnable PoC for your team. High level plan:

1) PoC runbook (PDF) — operator playbook for a 2‑day pilot (install, config, verify, thermal test, teardown).
2) Maintenance & patching plan — patch window examples, recommended rollbacks, and canary steps.
3) Switchover scenarios — description + ops commands for primary->failover and emergency teardown.
4) Credential rotation note — steps for KMS/HSM integration and zero‑downtime rotation approach.
5) Network diagram — minimal egress list + ports and endpoints.

Irene (cc) will assemble the runbook and the diagram. Rishi, can you add the oncall/ops SLA language and the operator matrix? We plan to attach three files and a one‑page executive summary for procurement.

We should be able to deliver initial artifacts by Thursday EOD (2025‑04‑24) and can schedule a 45‑minute walkthrough next Friday. If you need it sooner, tell us which pieces take priority.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415‑555‑0182
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alice Dunne <alice.dunne@pivothealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-20T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request for PoC proof-of-operation and maintainability details

Hi all —

Attaching the first draft of the PoC runbook (redwood_poc_runbook_v1.pdf) and a simple network diagram (network_diagram_vpc_revA.png). Highlights included in the runbook:

- Preflight checklist (OS images, firewall rules, KMS credentials, NTP)
- Installer steps (airgapped installer options and interactive vs unattended)
- Verify steps (smoke tests for inference latency, KV cache integrity, telemetry dry runs)
- Teardown procedure (graceful shutdown + state export)

On credential rotation: we support KMS integrations (customer KMS) and an in‑place rotation approach where new keys are staged, token caches drained, and cache rehydration is validated; operators can complete rotation in <15 minutes with monitored tailing of logs. We included an operator oncall matrix (operator_oncall_matrix.xlsx) showing 24/7 rotation and escalation steps.

Ben — I left notes where we should add concrete RTO/RPO numbers. Rishi, can you draft the maintenance window language and a sample SLA paragraph for procurement?

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alice Dunne <alice.dunne@pivothealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-21T13:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request for PoC proof-of-operation and maintainability details

Alice — quick draft of the maintenance & SLA language below (will include in the one‑pager):

- Planned maintenance windows: customers can schedule monthly maintenance windows; typical suggested window is 2 hours during off‑peak with rolling node updates to preserve availability.
- Emergency maintenance & security patching: critical patches can be applied within 24 hours with operator coordination; rollback steps are documented in section 4 of the runbook.
- RTO/RPO: for the reference PoC topology (single‑region, 3 node pool with persistent KV store) we target RTO <= 15 minutes for control plane failover and RPO <= 1 minute for inference state (KV cache warmup strategies). We will supply concrete test logs after the PoC.
- Escalation: oncall -> senior oncall -> engineering pager; contact matrix included in operator_oncall_matrix.xlsx.

I also added a short checklist of acceptance criteria the Pivot security team can sign off on after the pilot (node hardening, network egress validation, KMS integration validated).

If that aligns, we can wrap everything into a single PDF and join your procurement packet.

-rishi
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@pivothealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Dunne <alice.dunne@pivothealth.com>, procurement@pivothealth.com
Date: 2025-04-23T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request for PoC proof-of-operation and maintainability details

Marissa / team —

This looks good and addresses the security team's initial concerns. A few minor asks before procurement attaches this to the RFP: 

1) Can you add a single page that explicitly lists outbound domains/IPs and ports for the installer and optional telemetry (we need that for our firewall change request).
2) In the PoC runbook, under "credential rotation", can you include the exact CLI commands an operator would run (or a script) when integrating with an AWS KMS key?
3) For the RTO/RPO assertion, can you provide a short excerpt of the last internal run (timestamps + logs) demonstrating the sub-15 minute recovery? Redact internal IPs if needed.

If you can add these three items by EOD Monday we'll accept the packet for procurement. Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Tom
Senior Infrastructure Manager, Pivot Health
